title: The MCP server's ZDX deep-trace tools and troubleshooting prompt: inputs, results and mismatches

prose.text: The MCP server wraps the Python SDK's ZDX troubleshooting calls as tools and ships a guided prompt that chains them. Its general behavior is in [[shared.mcp-server]]; this subject covers the ZDX deep-trace tools.

checks.do: Whether the started trace's ID came from the tool result, which comes back empty, or from a follow-up listing.
Whether the server was started with write tools enabled before a start or delete was attempted.
Whether calls built from the guided prompt use the registered tool arguments rather than the prompt's `search` and string IDs.

start-tool-inputs.statement: The MCP start tool takes `device_id` as a string, `app_id`, `web_probe_id` and `cloudpath_probe_id` as integers, `session_length_minutes` defaulting to 5 and `probe_device` defaulting to true.

quotes: device_id: Annotated[str, Field(description="ZDX device ID (string, even if numeric).")]
int, Field(description="Application ID as an INTEGER (from zdx_list_applications).")
int, Field(description="Web probe ID as an INTEGER (from zdx_get_web_probes).")
Field(description="Cloud-path probe ID as an INTEGER (from zdx_list_cloudpath_probes)."),
Field(default=5, description="Session duration in minutes. Supported: 5, 15, 30, 60."),
Field(default=True, description="Probe the device for CPU/memory/disk/network metrics."),

start-tool-coerces.statement: The start tool converts the three IDs to integers and passes `session_name`, `app_id`, `web_probe_id`, `cloudpath_probe_id`, `session_length_minutes` and `probe_device` to the Python `start_deeptrace`.

start-tool-trace-id.statement: The tool reads the trace ID from the SDK result's `trace_id`, `traceId` or `id` and falls back to `started` for the status; since the Python start result carries none of those keys, the tool returns no trace ID and the status `started` whatever the API answered.
start-tool-trace-id.conditions: Follows from the tool's key lookup against the attributes the Python result model exposes; not observed against a live tenant.

write-gating.statement: The start and delete tools are disabled unless the operator passes `--write-tools`, and the server bridge confirms a delete before the tool body runs.

quotes: These are the write half of the read-heavy ZDX troubleshooting surface.
The delete is confirmed by the server bridge BEFORE the tool body runs;
Write tools are disabled unless the operator passes ``--write-tools``.

delete-requires-ids.statement: The delete tool refuses a call without both `device_id` and `trace_id`.

quotes: raise ValueError("device_id and trace_id are required for delete")

list-tool-records.statement: The deep-trace list tool returns each trace's SDK record (`as_dict()`) as one row, and the get tool returns the first element of the SDK's result, so their fields are whatever the Python models expose.

quotes: raw = result[0].as_dict() if result and len(result) > 0 else {}

timestamp-conversion.statement: Among the ZDX tools, only the analysis reader converts epoch timestamps to ISO strings (`convert_timestamps`); the deep-trace get tool's docstring says its timestamps are ISO-normalized, but its body passes the SDK record through unconverted.

quotes: unwrapped, timestamps ISO-normalized, and shaped to the identity fields.
raw = result[0].as_dict() if result and len(result) > 0 else {}

timestamp-conversion.conditions: A search of `src/zscaler_mcp/` at the pin finds `convert_timestamps(` called only in `deeptrace_analysis.py`.

probe-since.statement: The device and probe tools take `since` as an optional look-back in hours of at least 1, described as defaulting to 2 hours in ZDX.

quotes: Field(default=None, ge=1, description="Look-back window in HOURS (ZDX default 2h)."),
Field(default=None, ge=1, description="Look-back window in HOURS (ZDX default 2h)."),

prompt-search-arg.statement: The ZDX troubleshooting prompt tells the agent to call `zdx_list_devices(search=...)`, but the device-list tool's input has no `search` field; it filters by emails, user IDs, MAC address, private IPv4, location, department, geolocation, `since` and `offset`.
prompt-search-arg.conditions: The nine quoted fields are every field `ListDevicesInput` declares at the pin; how the server treats an undeclared argument was not traced.

prompt-string-ids.statement: The prompt also says to pass all IDs as strings, which disagrees with the start tool's integer application and probe IDs.
prompt-string-ids.conditions: A comparison of the prompt text with the start tool's input model.
